page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a storage-optimized and memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 23,038 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for small-block cached reads is also in the top tier, while large-block uncached reads and writes fall into the strong category. Database operations, evaluated via Redis SET benchmarks, reach top-tier throughput at 122.77 million operations per second. However, single-threaded tasks show moderate performance, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the average tier.

The high density of local NVMe storage combined with 768.0 GB of RAM makes this instance highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive local scratch space or large-scale database hosting without the latency of network-attached storage. The lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it demonstrates strong to top-tier prompt processing speeds for small and medium language models. This server is best suited for large relational databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, data warehousing, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server from the Lasv4 family, powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 96 vCPUs, 768.0 GB of RAM, and 23,038 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and exceptional memory bandwidth. Benchmarks highlight its strength in database operations, with Redis SET throughput reaching the top tier, alongside strong large-block memory read and write speeds. While single-threaded performance remains average, its massive local storage and high memory capacity make it highly efficient for data-intensive workloads. It is best suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput caching layers, and data warehousing.
